newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Resigning Hungary central banker lambasts govt.
newsitem.headline: Resigning Hungary central banker lambasts govt.

text.p: A top National Bank of Hungary (NBH) official who offered to resign on Monday over an unfavourable foreign exchange contract said he had done so because of unfair criticism from the government.
"When there are discrepancies about fundamental things then resignation is the only possibility," NBH vice president Frigyes Harshegyi told Reuters.

Harshegyi and fellow NBH vice-president Sandor Czirjak offered their resignations after disclosure of an unfavourable foreign exchange contract with Creditanstalt, concluded in 1992, that could cost the NBH more than three billion forints, newspapers said on Monday.
The contract was for foreign exchange rate guarantees maturing in 1998 that forced the NBH to create substantial risk reserves that have proven extremely costly, the reports said.
An internal report by the NBH said "a professional mistake was made" by those responsible for the contract and added that Czirjak and Harshegyi were "personally responsible".
The government discussed the report last week in a cabinet meeting and said that although the two vice presidents had worked effectively at the bank, action must be taken.
Harshegyi told Reuters he was being wrongly singled out for one decision at the expense of his overall record.

"One should not be judged over one decision which may have a positive or negative effect but on one's overall performance," he said. "If it is normal practice to assess a high-ranking official on the basis of one single decision why should I carry on?".
Harshegyi added that he had not yet finally resigned but was likely to do so on Tuesday, when an official announcement will be made.
"Most probably I will (resign) tomorrow. Mr Czirjak and I will probably terminate our jobs at the year-end."
Both Czirjak and Harshegyi have been NBH vice presidents since 1991.
The reports of a huge loss in a government contract came hard on the heels of a scandal over payments of millions of dollars to a consultant at privatisation agency APV Rt.
That revelation led to the dismissal of the entire APV board and the minister in charge.
